    "articleBody" : "The farmers’ agitation that disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Bengaluru National Highway-48 for more than 61 hours ended early Friday (November 6) after sugar mill owners agreed to a payment formula offering sugarcane growers up to Rs 4,200 per tonne. The Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana, led by Raju Shetti, called off its protest following an agreement reached late Thursday night (November 6).  Sugar mills agree to Rs 4,200 per tonne formula  The meeting took place at the Kolhapur district collector’s office in the presence of Minister Hasan Mushrif and representatives of sugar factories. Shetti, who had sought Rs 4,500 per tonne, agreed to the revised amount, reported the Indian Express.Also Read: Karnataka sugarcane stir intensifies as farmers launch ‘Jail Bharo’ protest in Belagavi“The formula has been finalised. Farmers will receive an initial payment of Rs 3,900 per tonne, followed by Rs 100 at the end of the crushing season. The remaining Rs 200 will be paid before the next crushing season, provided sugar prices remain stable at Rs 45 per kg,” Shetti said.If sugar prices cross Rs 45 per kg, farmers will receive 70 per cent of the additional revenue, while factory owners will get the remaining 30 per cent, stated the report.  Protest ends, traffic begins returning to normal  Shetti announced the end of the agitation at the Kini toll plaza and in Satara around 1 am on Friday. A strike planned for Friday was also withdrawn. Traffic on the Pune-Satara-Kolhapur stretch of NH-48 began returning to normal.Also Read: Sugarcane farmers block highways in Karnataka, demand higher pricesThe blockade had affected nearly 120 km between Nagthane in Satara district and Sangli Phata in Kolhapur district. Scores of heavy vehicles were stranded. Traffic diversions resulted in congestion also on smaller roads. Commuters travelling towards Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara and Belagavi had to deal with severe delays. The agitation also left more than 1,500 trucks carrying essential goods stranded, according to Maharashtra State Transporters Association president Baba Shinde.The backdrop   The agitation comes after nearly two months of protests by sugarcane growers in Maharashtra, who have been demanding a better price for their produce. Farmers have accused the state government and sugar mill owners of ignoring their demands.  Farmers in Satara later joined the agitation and warned that they would intensify the protest if their demands were not accepted.  ",

The Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana, led by Raju Shetti, called off its protest following an agreement reached late Thursday night (November 6).  </p><h2>Sugar mills agree to Rs 4,200 per tonne formula  </h2><p>The meeting took place at the Kolhapur district collector’s office in the presence of Minister Hasan Mushrif and representatives of sugar factories. Shetti, who had sought Rs 4,500 per tonne, agreed to the revised amount, reported the <i>Indian Express</i>.</p><p><b>Also Read:</b> <a href="https://thefederal.com/category/states/south/karnataka/karnataka-sugarcane-stir-intensifies-farmers-launch-jail-bharo-protest-261614" target="_blank">Karnataka sugarcane stir intensifies as farmers launch ‘Jail Bharo’ protest in Belagavi</a></p><p>“The formula has been finalised. Farmers will receive an initial payment of Rs 3,900 per tonne, followed by Rs 100 at the end of the crushing season. The remaining Rs 200 will be paid before the next crushing season, provided sugar prices remain stable at Rs 45 per kg,” Shetti said.</p><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_1_before_before"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-before" id="inside_post_content_ad_1_before"></div><div role="region" aria-label="Advertisement" class="hide inside-post-ad-1 inside-post-ad ads_common_inside_post" id="inside_post_content_ad_1"></div><div class="hide inside-post-ad-after" id="inside_post_content_ad_1_after"></div><p>If sugar prices cross Rs 45 per kg, farmers will receive 70 per cent of the additional revenue, while factory owners will get the remaining 30 per cent, stated the report.  </p><h2>Protest ends, traffic begins returning to normal  </h2><p>Shetti announced the end of the agitation at the Kini toll plaza and in Satara around 1 am on Friday. A strike planned for Friday was also withdrawn. Traffic on the Pune-Satara-Kolhapur stretch of NH-48 began returning to normal.</p><p><b>Also Read:</b> <a href="https://thefederal.com/category/states/south/karnataka/sugarcane-farmers-karnataka-259417" target="_blank">Sugarcane farmers block highways in Karnataka, demand higher prices</a></p><p>The blockade had affected nearly 120 km between Nagthane in Satara district and Sangli Phata in Kolhapur district. Scores of heavy vehicles were stranded. Traffic diversions resulted in congestion also on smaller roads. Commuters travelling towards Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara and Belagavi had to deal with severe delays. The agitation also left more than 1,500 trucks carrying essential goods stranded, according to Maharashtra State Transporters Association president Baba Shinde.</p><h2>The backdrop   </h2><p>The agitation comes after nearly two months of protests by sugarcane growers in Maharashtra, who have been demanding a better price for their produce. Farmers have accused the state government and sugar mill owners of ignoring their demands.  </p><p>Farmers in Satara later joined the agitation and warned that they would intensify the protest if their demands were not accepted.  </p><!-- !{data.story}--></div></div></div></div></div><div id="news_buzz_updates_before" class="extra-elements hide"></div><div id="news_buzz_updates" class="extra-elements hide"></div><div id="news_buzz_updates_after" class="extra-elements hide"></div><div id="before_tags" class=" to-be-async-loaded-ad before_tags"></div><div class="mid_section_menu m_top15 all-tags-wrapper"><span class="catTag_hover tag-article-name"><a href="https://thefederal.com/tags/sugarcane-farmers" rel="follow" class="sub_category_button_three">Sugarcane farmers</a></span><span class="catTag_hover tag-article-name"><a href="https://thefederal.com/tags/road-blockade" rel="follow" class="sub_category_button_three">Road blockade</a></span></div><div id="after_tags" class=" hide"></div><nav aria-label="Article Pagination" class="page-pager pagi_wrap undefined"></nav><div class="clearfix"></div><section aria-label="Comments" class="comments-accordion hide"><div style="text-align:center;margin: 15px auto;" class="comments-section-wrap"><button id="comments-btn" data-url="https://thefederal.com/category/states/west/maharashtra/maharashtra-farmers-end-nh-48-blockade-as-sugar-mills-accept-rs-4200-per-tonne-formula-262019" aria-label="Comments">Comments</button></div><div id="comments" class="hide"></div></section><div id="ad_after_comments" class=" hide"></div></div></div><style>.all-quiz-wrapper {

did not want to cause further inconvenience to festive travellers.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="2"></span>Shetti said his demand for a sugar cane rate of Rs 4,200 per tonne had effectively been met, though not in a single instalment as originally sought.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="4"></span>“Kolhapur collector is going to give the assurance as proposed by sugar mills in writing. Same will be applicable for Sangli and Satara districts,” Shetti said while announcing the withdrawal of the highway blockade.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="6"></span>Earlier in the evening, sugar millers from Kolhapur proposed paying Rs 3,900 per tonne as the first instalment, an additional Rs 100 per tonne at the end of the crushing season and another Rs 200 per tonne if sugar prices remained stable at Rs 45 per kg.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="11"></span>If factory-gate sugar prices exceeded Rs 45 per kg, the additional revenue would be shared in a 70:30 ratio between farmers and millers, the proposal stated.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="13"></span>Responding to the proposal, Shetti had said, “I will discuss the proposal with my representatives who attended the meeting and then decide whether to continue the blockade or withdraw.”<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="15"></span>The three-day agitation had severely disrupted Diwali   var name = cname + '=';
  var ca = document.cookie.split(';');
  for (var i = 0; i < ca.length; i++) {

    while (c.charAt(0) == ' ') {

    }
    if (c.indexOf(name) == 0) {
      return c.substring(name.length, c.length);
    }
  }
  return '';
}

Summary of this article

  • The Pune-Bengaluru highway remained blocked for a third day as farmers demanded a ₹4,500-per-tonne advance for sugarcane.

  • The protest disrupted traffic across a 120-km stretch, leaving heavy vehicles stranded and clogging diversion routes.

  • MSRTC cancelled around 100 bus trips daily; transporters said more than 1,500 trucks carrying goods were stuck.

The Pune-Bengaluru National Highway (NH-48) remained blocked for a third consecutive day on Thursday as farmers led by former MP Raju Shetti continued their agitation for an advance payment of ₹4,500 per tonne of sugarcane.

The blockade has disrupted traffic along nearly 120 km between Nagthane in Satara district and Sangli Phata in Kolhapur district. Heavy vehicles remained stranded, while traffic diverted onto bypasses and smaller roads caused congestion across the region. Commuters travelling towards Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara and Belagavi were affected.

“We have been stuck on the highway since last night with our children and elderly family members. We were travelling to Kolhapur to celebrate Diwali with our relatives, but our vehicle has barely moved for hours. We have limited food and water, and the children are getting restless,” said Mangesh Chirute, a passenger stranded on the highway, as reported by Hinudstan Times.

Diversions Push Traffic Onto Smaller Roads

Vehicles travelling from Pune towards Kolhapur and Sangli faced heavy congestion between the D-Mart area in Satara and Ajintha Chowk. Authorities diverted traffic through Rahimatpur, but heavy trucks on the alternative route slowed movement further and made it difficult for smaller vehicles to pass.

Small vehicles heading towards Sangli have been advised to travel through Satara city and take the Rahimatpur route, then continue via Pusesavali and Palus. Motorists going to Kolhapur can use routes through Rahimatpur, including roads connecting Ashta in Sangli district, Bagani and Peth Vadgaon. These routes are also facing increasing pressure, and authorities have urged commuters to check road conditions before setting out.

By Outlook News Desk

MSRTC Cancels About 100 Trips A Day

The blockade has disrupted bus services as well. The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) has cancelled around 100 trips daily.

“We had already started operating some buses through alternative routes from Wednesday, including via Sangli, Rahimatpur and Vita, to ensure that passengers stranded on the way could reach their destinations,” said Arun Siya, MSRTC Pune divisional controller.

“We are constantly assessing which routes can safely be used to operate services and hope that a solution will emerge soon,” he said.

The diversion routes have also raised safety concerns. Siya said a Karnataka-registered bus was stopped near Rahimatpur, beyond Satara, on Thursday and its window panes were damaged.

Trucks Carrying Essential Goods Remain Stranded

The protest has held up commercial transport and deliveries of essential goods. More than 1,500 trucks carrying grains, vegetables and other commodities have been stranded for two days, said Baba Shinde, president of the Maharashtra State Transporters Association.

“The prolonged blockade is causing major losses to transporters and could also affect the supply chain if the situation continues,” Shinde told Hindustan Times

Farmers Seek Higher Cane Payment

The Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana is demanding a minimum first instalment of ₹4,500 per tonne for sugarcane supplied to mills during the current crushing season. It says mills earn substantial revenue from sugar, ethanol and other by-products but do not share a fair proportion with growers.

The organisation has also sought an increase in the minimum selling price of sugar from ₹31 to ₹50 per kg and a revision of ethanol procurement prices. It has warned that it will intensify the agitation if farmers and sugar factories fail to reach an agreement.

By Pranay Vatsa

Fadnavis Urges Farmers To End Agitation

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has appealed to farmers to call off the protest peacefully. He said the government fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP), while payments above that rate must be negotiated between sugar factories and farmers.

Fadnavis said Minister Hasan Mushrif had been asked to hold talks with stakeholders. Discussions involving sugar industry representatives and experts are also expected at the Sugar Commissioner’s office in Pune.

Farmers, commuters and transport operators are awaiting a settlement as negotiations continue and the highway remains disrupted.
